questions.question: Explain why Mapungubwe is called the first state in southern Africa.
questions.expected_answer: From about 1220 to 1300 AD, Mapungubwe was ruled by one central king with power over many people and a large area, including smaller settlements with their own chiefs who were under his authority. The king had advisers, controlled trade and wealth, settled disputes and led ceremonies, and society was divided into classes.

questions.question: What is meant by sacred leadership at Mapungubwe?
questions.expected_answer: The king was not only a political leader but also a spiritual one. He was believed to be closest to the ancestors and able to ask them for rain and to protect the land and the people. Because he was sacred, he lived apart from ordinary people on top of the hill and was treated with great respect.

questions.question: Give three reasons why the king lived on top of Mapungubwe Hill, and explain the purpose of the stone walls.
questions.expected_answer: Living high up showed his high status, it separated the sacred king from ordinary people, it was easy to protect because of the steep cliffs, and the hill may have had spiritual importance. The stone walls did not hold up houses; they marked out and separated important spaces such as the royal area and showed the king's power.
